Output 1: Green jobs created for women and youth to rebuild resilient livelihoods during and after COVID-19. Results attained under output 1 (one): The livelihood capacity of over 200 youth and women (majority of whom are ex-poachers) around targeted conservation areas in areas of Kibale, Rwenzori, Bwindi, and Lake Mburo was strengthened. UNDP in partnership with Uganda Wildlife Authority (UWA) equipped them with the skills and tools to pursue alternative livelihoods such as apiary farming (Apiculture).
Output 2: Stimulus packages for the green recovery targeting MSMEs. Results attained under output two (2) With UNDPs support, a new sports tourism product - Rwenzori Marathon - was developed. The product pioneered in Kasese was a collective effort by UNDP, Uganda Wildlife Authority and the private sector to diversify Uganda’s tourism product range by harnessing the country’s rich topography; broaden meaningful community participation in the tourism value chain and drive domestic and international tourist traffic to experience the enchanted adventure that the Rwenzori offers. In addition, UNDP supported the development of the Rwenzori Mountain Royal expedition documentary to promote mountaineering tourism in the Rwenzoris whilst amplifying the conversation about the need to tackle biodiversity loss and the impact of climate change on the Rwenzori Mountain ranges.
Output 3: Strategic policy reorientation towards inclusive green recovery, risk-informed development and enhanced national system capacities. Results attained under output three (3) UNDP fostered a platform to rethink and explore the imperatives to stimulate recovery and drive the resilience agenda of the tourism industry in these unprecedented times of planetary crisis, conflict and disease. The platform also brought to the fore the consequences of climate change for Uganda; and the need for climate action including imperatives green recovery stimulus packages targeting SMEs.
UNDP also supported the Government to prepare the Regulatory Impact Assessment of the Tourism Bill 2022 to inform decisions by Cabinet of Uganda on the proposed amendment to the Tourism Act 2008.
